message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo, fought on 18 June 1815, was one of the bloodiest single-day engagements of the Napoleonic Wars.  While exact figures vary by source, the generally accepted totals are:

| Side | Approximate casualties (killed, wounded, missing) |
|------|---------------------------------------------------|
| **Allied (British, Dutch, Belgian, Prussian)** | **≈ 25 000** |
| **French** | **≈ 25 000** |

**Breakdown (approximate)**  

| Category | Allied | French |
|----------|--------|--------|
| Killed | ~ 4 000 | ~ 4 000 |
| Wounded | ~ 12 000 | ~ 12 000 |
| Missing/Prisoners | ~ 9 000 | ~ 9 000 |

These numbers come from contemporary reports and later military historians.  For instance, the British Army’s official casualty list records 4,000 killed, 12,000 wounded, and 9,000 missing, while French sources give similar figures.  The combined total of roughly 50 000 casualties (including both sides) underscores why Waterloo is remembered as a decisive and costly victory for the Seventh Coalition.
